THE CENSUS HAS CROSSED ITS REFUSAL CEILING, AND HERE IS THE FIRST PER-STUDY ATTRIBUTION.

    1278.160 s at 2026-09-06T04:00:44Z, against a 1200 s CENSUS_REFUSAL_SECS.

The trend, newest first: 1278.160, 1142.235, 1070.850, 1060.274, 1019.092, 973.508, 873.277. That is +46% in four days. The 1000 s ALARM was crossed days ago and nothing acted on it, because the alarm only prints; the refusal is the one that stops a delivery, and it stopped campaign/the-lot's.

THE SPLIT LANDED THIS MORNING AND THIS IS ITS FIRST USE. Before it, a census was one number and "profile it" meant starting from scratch. Now:

    the-census study     673.0 s   52.7%   cpu_ratio 36.70
    the-meeting study    297.2 s   23.3%   cpu_ratio 36.11
    everything else      307.9 s   24.1%   <- the serial tail
    total               1278.2 s

TWO THINGS THAT READS OUT IMMEDIATELY.

First, the two studies are BOTH running at cpu_ratio ~36 on 40 cores, which is close to saturated. They are not where a parallelism win lives. The remaining 307.9 s is, and it is 24% of the run: that is the fraction executing at low parallelism, and it matches the ~220 s tail at ratio ~4.5 measured on this box earlier. A census that saturated its tail the way its studies do would land back under the ceiling on its own.

Second, census-of-the-meeting costs 297 s of every census, 23% of the total, every time. That is a real price on a study whose job is to prove a property -- that two identical-but-for-name rosters place identically -- rather than to measure a moving quantity. Worth knowing before anyone argues about the ceiling, because dropping or sampling it is a 23% cut available without profiling anything.

WHAT THE TEST FORBIDS, and it is right to. Its message says: "Raising this number needs the attribution, the optimisable share, and the condition for ratcheting back down -- see the doc on CENSUS_REFUSAL_SECS, and the f7496156 / e0a2e988 precedent." So the ceiling is not a knob to turn to unblock a campaign. The attribution above is the first of the three things it asks for; the optimisable share and the ratchet-down condition are not established yet and I am not claiming them.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE RIGHT NOW: no census can deliver until this is resolved. Any campaign whose close needs a census refresh is blocked, and it will present as a rc=4 "COMMIT REFUSED" with the run's own output stranded in hornvale-census-wt. Preserve that output before the next census resets the worktree -- two runs are already preserved under ~/.local/state/hornvale/stranded/.
